Any swap-funded top-up remains unvalidated and must include round-trip venue fees and lender repayment.

flashRelevance.danglingStakeAuthority: Capital-independent. Borrowed SOL/USDC/LST cannot make an outsider the canonical stake staker required by DepositStake.
flashRelevance.delegatedVictimToken: Capital-independent until a compatible same-mint top-up exists. Unrelated flash assets cannot authorize transfer/burn of a victim token account. Each current victim source is individually below the 1 SOL stake split threshold.
flashRelevance.onrampHarvest: Capital-sensitive, but the only successful exact-state sequence used already-active stake and unavailable live signers. Fresh SOL stake cannot become fully active/merge-compatible in the same epoch. No direct current same-mint lender was available; no signed DEX buy/replenish/sell/unwind/repay route was established.
flashRelevance.multiProviderStatus: The four-provider signed v1 envelope fits 1,773 bytes/39 addresses/16 instructions, but all stack cases are blocker evidence, not successful flash controls. Therefore no validated flash-wrapped drain is claimed.

compute.conclusion: 239,519 CU is below the observed 1,400,000-CU simulation envelope; compute was not the blocker.

findings: The two withdrawer-only HHZn stake accounts are not bearer deposits: signed exact-clone DepositStake fails because the staker is not the canonical PDA.
All 34 delegated-token candidates fail at their current maximum burnable balance; the two dominant balances remain below the one-SOL split threshold and failed atomically.

Permissionless Replenish creates a reproducible value-transfer opportunity for a depositor holding already-active same-vote stake, but outsider exploitability was not validated because the exact live user signers and a compatible signed flash acquisition/unwind route were unavailable.
Operator-only metadata/update paths are non-findings for outsider threat modeling.
infeasibleOrUnvalidated: A mainnet sigVerify:true diagnostic with someone else's stake/token authority is cryptographically impossible without their private key; signed tests therefore used an exact-account Surfpool fork and fresh attacker key.

Failed mainnet simulations returned null requested post accounts; atomic rollback follows Solana transaction semantics and was additionally checked through signed fork failure controls. No transaction was sent.
No successful tri-/four-source flash composition was obtained. The largest signed provider-stack envelope fit the byte/account limits but failed before complete repayment.
A same-transaction fresh-stake route is infeasible because the stake activation epoch cannot match an already-active pool/onramp in that transaction.
